text: Same 8 tickets as the plan. Doing the plan's way A: one `put` per ticket, then read each back.
All 8 writes landed, each adding only the Topics line. Checking the list, then clearing the queue entry and the ticket.

I took the one queued task, "Give every ticket that has no Topics line one", and it's done. All 8 tickets without topics now have a `Topics:` line. I used the topics the ticket's plan proposed:

| Ticket | Topics |
|---|---|
| dashboard-architecture-plan | dashboard, modularity |
| dashboard-architecture | dashboard, modularity |
| cursor-parity-checklist | the-framework, cursor-parity |
| skill-browser-access | skills, browser |
| cold-read-follow-ups | skills, docs |
| actions-agent-two-branch-names | agent-driver, branches |
| ac-enforcement-merge-gate | system-prompt, merge-gate |
| dashboard-ux-notes | dashboard, UX |

- **Checked:** I read each ticket back after writing it, and the new line was the only change. The ticket list now has no open ticket without topics.
- **No pull request:** only ticket files changed, and each change is its own commit pushed straight to `agent-data`.
- **Closed it myself:** I removed the queue entry and closed the ticket, which also dropped my claim. Normally a merged pull request closes a ticket, but this task had none.
- **Queue is empty now.**

One thing to watch: when a ticket's GitHub issue changes, the ticket import may rewrite that ticket without its new line. If topics go missing after the next import, the fix in the plan is to have the skills that write tickets always add a `Topics:` line, as its own ticket.
